newsitem.title: INDIA: India state-run banks seen improving in 96/97-RBI.
newsitem.headline: India state-run banks seen improving in 96/97-RBI.

text.p: State-run banks would post better results for 1996/97 (April-March) than in the previous year on account of lower provisions towards depreciation on government securities, the head of India's central bank said on Monday.
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor Chakravarty Rangarajan said the rate of interest on government securities during 1996/97 had shown a fall from the previous year's levels.

"It may not, therefore, be necessary for the banks to provide any significant additional provisions on account of depreciation on government securities during 1996/97," he told a bank economists' meeting at Mahabaleshwar town in western India.
"The working results of the public sector (state-run) banks during 1996/97 will, to that extent alone, show higher profits."
Rangarajan said results of state-run banks for the half year ended September 30, 1996 showed operating profits of 43.12 billion rupees against 35.07 billion in the corresponding period last year.
Operating profits of state-run banks were expected to be around 98.8 billion rupees as of March 31, 1997 against 75.72 billion for the previous year, he added.
